dedupe_keys.name: cmap transportation resilience improvement plan flood and heat exposure and risk scores for chicago region transport assets

description: The Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP) publishes the asset data behind its Transportation Resilience Improvement Plan (TRIP) as open layers on its Data Hub. Coverage: 16 layers for the Chicago region, giving flooding exposure for all bus routes, CTA bus stops, CTA and Metra rail stations and lines, Pace bus stops, culverts, roads, bridges, garages and yards and regional trails, and heat and cold exposure for CTA and Metra rail lines and stations. The CTA rail station layer has 144 stations with lines, average daily rides, access to employment and freight clusters, emergency facilities within half a mile, zero-car households, Social Vulnerability Index values, a flood exposure score and a final score. CMAP computes a risk score for each asset as 60% exposure plus 40% criticality, with exposure indicators adjusted for future climate and criticality from historical data. Format and access: an ArcGIS feature service with a Data Hub page and an interactive web map. Licence and cost: free and not restricted; users should cite CMAP. Caveats: scores are relative screening values and the weighting is a planning choice. The asset scores can set flood and heat hazard exposure and criticality weights in transit resilience and climate adaptation models. It relates to the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index and the National Transit Database in the catalogue.
